# Spec §11 — decisions: Audio (the owner's audio pass, from 2026-10-30)

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

The owner's pass over a clip's sound, begun 2026-10-30 to turn a desktop USB microphone's
recording into usable audio for a video. Its IDs are the AU- series. Each was recorded before
its code.

- **AU-1 — `audio.volume`'s ceiling is ×32 (+30.1 dB), not ×4; the Volume slider keeps its
  0–400 % travel and the field beside it takes the rest (owner, 2026-10-30: "400% should not be
  a hard max").** The owner's recording `samples/Rode-usb-mic.m4a` (a RØDE USB microphone,
  30.4 s of AAC mono at 48 kHz) peaks at −18.6 dBFS with an integrated loudness of −44.7 LUFS
  (ffmpeg's `volumedetect` and `ebur128`), so Normalize wanted ×7.55 to reach −1 dBFS and stopped
  at ×4, −6.5 dBFS. The ceiling stays — `MAX_GAIN` still bounds `check_audio`'s refusal,
  `clamp_audio` and the envelope, so one bad patch cannot send +80 dB to the mix — but at ×32:
  Normalize now reaches −1 dBFS from a peak as quiet as −31.1 dBFS, and 30 dB covers the gap
  between this microphone's −44.7 LUFS and a −14 LUFS delivery. 32 rather than 31.62 (exactly
  +30 dB) so the refusal reads a whole number: "audio.volume must be between 0 and 32".
  - Measured before the change: AVFoundation's audio mix applies a `setVolumeRamp` volume above
    4 exactly. The recording read through `AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput` in 32-bit float peaks at
    4.000, 7.600, 16.000, 32.000 and 64.000 times its ×1 peak at those volumes (a scratch probe
    of 2026-10-30), so ×4 was the model's rule and nothing beneath it changes.
  - The Volume row: the slider keeps 0–400 %, where its resolution is useful (a 0–3200 % rail
    would put 100 % at a thirty-second of its width); the field takes 0–3200 %. A value above
    400 % pins the knob at the rail's end, and a drag writes the rail's own range. The quick
    picks are unchanged.
  - One Swift copy of the ceiling, `AudioNormalize.maxGain`, which the Volume row's field and
    the agent's sentences now read too, is held to the core's refusal by `core/tests/audio_gain.rs`,
    reading its `static let` line as `graphic_ffi.rs` reads `maxTextureSide`. No `rc_*` export:
    `ReelCore.swift` is over its cap, and one constant does not need the FFI.
  - No format bump. The file's shape is unchanged and the reader runs no range check
    (`Project::validate` does not call `check_audio`), so an older build opens a project with a
    volume above 4, plays it at ×4 through `audio.rs`'s clamp and writes the stored number back
    unchanged. A bump guards against a loss on that round trip, and there is none.
  - What it accepts: a mix can go further past full scale than before. The preview's output and
    an un-normalised export clip there (phase 5d's 16-bit decode, which says so); a normalised
    export gains in float (#86) and does not. Normalize itself still lands at −1 dBFS.

AU-2…AU-4 open road map "audio" (`designs/audio.md`, from `designs/audio-survey.md`'s tiers A
and B), recorded at its AP0 from the owner's answers of 2026-10-30 to the road map's five
choices ("Yes, lift scopes, and allow Apple's built-in audio effects", then "OK" to each of the
rest), before any of its code. **Numbering from here:** each phase records its decisions in a
block of its own, APn's as AU-n0…AU-n9 (AP1's AU-10…, AP10's AU-100…), so phases built in
parallel lanes never claim one ID; AP0's are AU-2…AU-9.

- **AU-2 — Audio beyond what shipped is in scope: EQ, track and bus processing, and Apple's
  built-in audio units (owner, 2026-10-30, choice 1; amends spec §1).** Spec §1's non-goal
  "audio beyond what shipped … so no EQ, mix buses or Audio Units, while offline voice effects
  are deferred rather than out" is lifted. In: Frame Job's own DSP stages, track and master
  processing, and the audio units macOS itself ships (`AUSoundIsolation`, `AVAudioUnitEQ`, the
  dynamics and time-pitch units), run in the process as `AVAudioUnitTimePitch` already runs for
  speed-ramp audio. Out, under §1's plugin system: hosting third-party Audio Unit plug-ins (the
  survey's C5). Tier C of the survey is not in the road map; it is neither in nor out until the
  owner asks.
- **AU-3 — Live stages are Frame Job's own DSP in the tap, in one fixed order; Apple's units
  only where Frame Job cannot write its own (owner, 2026-10-30, choices 4 and 5).** EQ and the
  high-pass, the hum notch, the gate/expander, the de-esser and the limiter are written beside
  the compressor: real-time safe in the `MTAudioProcessingTap`, deterministic, and proved
  against analytic responses. Apple's units are used for ML voice isolation (`AUSoundIsolation`)
  and E8's voice effects, both rendered offline per clip window into `cache/` on the speed-ramp
  audio pattern. AP0's spike S1 may overturn the first half by measurement, recorded as an
  amendment here. The clip chain's order is fixed: channels → high-pass and EQ → hum notch →
  isolation or noise reduction → gate → de-esser → compressor → limiter, then the fader (the
  core's envelope). Every stage is off by default and inert when off, so a project that uses
  none plays and exports byte-identical to today (a track whose clips ask for nothing still
  gets no tap). A closed vocabulary, as R5-1 has every effect: no user-ordered chain, no
  per-clip stage list.
- **AU-4 — Normalize targets loudness: −16 LUFS by default at −1 dBTP, Peak kept beside it
  (owner, 2026-10-30, choices 2 and 3).** AP1 adds Normalize's Loudness mode (a target in
  LUFS, gated BS.1770 over the window that plays) beside today's Peak; the button stays Peak
  until AP2's limiter can hold −1 dBTP, and from AP2 its default is Loudness. The default
  target is −16 LUFS integrated, with −14 (YouTube's playback reference) and −23 (EBU R 128)
  as quick picks; the ceiling is −1 dBTP. `normalize_clip` keeps `peak_db` and gains the
  loudness mode's arguments.

  isolation or noise reduction → gate → de-esser → compressor → limiter, then the fader (the
  core's envelope). Every stage is off by default and inert when off, so a project that uses
  none plays and exports byte-identical to today (a track whose clips ask for nothing still
  gets no tap). A closed vocabulary, as R5-1 has every effect: no user-ordered chain, no
  per-clip stage list.
- **AU-4 — Normalize targets loudness: −16 LUFS by default at −1 dBTP, Peak kept beside it
  (owner, 2026-10-30, choices 2 and 3).** AP1 adds Normalize's Loudness mode (a target in
  LUFS, gated BS.1770 over the window that plays) beside today's Peak; the button stays Peak
  until AP2's limiter can hold −1 dBTP, and from AP2 its default is Loudness. The default
  target is −16 LUFS integrated, with −14 (YouTube's playback reference) and −23 (EBU R 128)
  as quick picks; the ceiling is −1 dBTP. `normalize_clip` keeps `peak_db` and gains the
  loudness mode's arguments.

42	/// |---|---|---|
43	/// | K-weighting gain at 1 kHz | +0.6977 dB | **+0.6977 dB** |
44	/// | 0 dBFS 997 Hz sine in ONE channel of a stereo pair | −3.01 LKFS | −3.010 LUFS |

48	/// | case 4, the absolute gate (10 s @ −72, 60 s @ −23, 10 s @ −72) | −23.0 LUFS | −23.015 LUFS |

54	/// second is the standard's own calibration sentence, quoted from § 2.1 of
55	/// Annex 1, and it is the tighter check of the two — it is stated at 997 Hz,
56	/// which is the frequency the offset cancels EXACTLY. The Tech 3341 cases

216	        // The cap is computed on TRUE peak rather than sample peak, and that
217	        // is what makes the write safe as well as honest: true peak is never
218	        // below sample peak, so a gain that keeps the true peak under the
219	        // ceiling keeps every 16-bit sample inside full scale, and the clip
220	        // in the writer's quantiser (`ExportAudioGain`) never has to fire.
221	        //
222	        // A peak that is not a finite number is NO headroom, which is the
223	        // safe answer and not the obvious one. −∞ cannot reach this line at
224	        // all — a nil `integratedLUFS` has already returned above, and a
225	        // programme with any block above Γa has a non-zero sample peak — so
226	        // the only value that gets here is a +∞ carried in from float source
227	        // media holding a non-finite sample, and "the peak cannot be
228	        // measured" has to mean "do not push it up". Infinite headroom would
229	        // mean the opposite: apply the whole requested boost and ignore the
230	        // ceiling.
231	        let headroom = measured.truePeakDBTP.isFinite ? ceiling - measured.truePeakDBTP : 0
232	        // The two are quantised DIFFERENTLY, because they mean different
233	        // things. `wanted` is a target and rounds to nearest: half a
234	        // hundredth of a decibel either way of a ±0.5 LU claim is nothing.
235	        // `headroom` is a CONSTRAINT — rounding it to nearest hands back up
236	        // to 0.005 dB of the attenuation the ceiling asked for, and a
237	        // ceiling-capped export then reports, and holds, a true peak ABOVE
238	        // the ceiling it names about half the time (which is what the sheet's
239	        // "capped so its true peak stays under −1 dBTP" would then be
240	        // promising falsely). It rounds DOWN, toward more attenuation, so the
241	        // shifted true peak can only land at or under the ceiling.
242	        let quantised = Swift.min(
243	            (wanted / gainStepDB).rounded() * gainStepDB,
244	            (headroom / gainStepDB).rounded(.down) * gainStepDB)
245	        return ExportLoudness(
246	            measured: measured, target: target, ceiling: ceiling,
247	            gainDB: quantised.isFinite ? quantised : 0, cappedByPeak: headroom < wanted)
248	    }
249	
250	    /// The one line every export reports: `"Peak −1.0 dBTP · −14.0 LUFS"`.
251	    var summary: String {
252	        guard truePeakDBTP.isFinite else {
253	            // −∞ is digital silence. Anything else non-finite is a mix
254	            // carrying a non-finite sample, and calling THAT silent is the
255	            // loudest lie this line could tell.
256	            return truePeakDBTP == -.infinity
257	                ? "Silent" : "Peak not measurable (a non-finite sample in the mix)"
258	        }
259	        let peak = "Peak \(Self.decibels(truePeakDBTP)) dBTP"
260	        let measurement: String
261	        if let integrated = integratedLUFS {
262	            measurement = "\(peak) · \(Self.decibels(integrated)) LUFS"
263	        } else {
264	            // A programme shorter than one 400 ms gating block, or one whose
265	            // every block fell under Γa. It has a peak and no loudness, and
266	            // saying which is better than printing −∞.
267	            measurement = "\(peak) · loudness not measurable"
268	        }
269	        guard mixClipped else { return measurement }
270	        // The figures are the mix's and the file's are worse, so the line
271	        // says which it is showing — in both consumers at once, since the
272	        // progress sheet's last line and the `export` tool's result are the
273	        // same string. `mixClipped` says why they differ at all.
274	        return "\(measurement) — measured on the mix, which clipped at +"
275	            + "\(Self.decibels(measured.samplePeakDBFS)) dBFS before it was written"
276	    }
277	
278	    /// One decimal, with the typographic minus the rest of the chrome uses.
279	    private static func decibels(_ value: Double) -> String {
280	        String(format: "%.1f", value).replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−")
281	    }
282	}
283	
284	// MARK: - The meter
285	
286	/// BS.1770-4 over a stream of interleaved 32-bit float frames.
287	///
288	/// Feed it every frame of the programme in order, then ask it once. The
289	/// K-weighting filters and the true-peak interpolator both carry state
290	/// ACROSS calls — that is the whole reason this is an object and not a
291	/// function: the filters run continuously over the programme (blocks
292	/// overlap by 75 %, so a per-block reset is not even well defined) and the
293	/// interpolating FIR needs 11 samples of per-channel history, which arrive
294	/// in one buffer and are needed in the next.
295	final class LoudnessMeter {
296	
297	    /// The rate the coefficient tables are published at, and the rate the
298	    /// export mix is decoded at. Not a default: `init` refuses anything else.
299	    static let requiredSampleRate: Double = 48000
300	
301	    /// Every measurement window BS.1770-4 § 2 names, in seconds.
302	    ///
303	    /// A gating block is 400 ms; blocks overlap by 75 %, so one starts every
304	    /// 100 ms and a block is exactly four consecutive 100 ms sub-blocks. That
305	    /// is why the accumulator below keeps a running sum per sub-block and a
306	    /// ring of the last four rather than re-summing 19 200 samples per block.
307	    private static let blockSeconds: Double = 0.400
308	    private static let hopSeconds: Double = 0.100
309	    private static let subBlocksPerBlock = 4
310	
311	    /// BS.1770-4 equation (2)'s offset. Note 1 of that clause says what it
312	    /// is for: it cancels the K-weighting's gain at 997 Hz, which this
313	    /// implementation measures as +0.6977 dB.
314	    private static let offset: Double = -0.691
315	
316	    /// Γa, the absolute gate, in LUFS. A block at or below it is not
317	    /// programme.
318	    private static let absoluteGate: Double = -70
319	
320	    /// Γr's offset below the gated mean, in LU.
321	    private static let relativeGate: Double = -10
322	
323	    // ---- K-weighting -----------------------------------------------------
324	
325	    /// One biquad, in the difference equation BS.1770-4's Fig. 3 draws:
326	    ///
327	    ///     y[n] = b0·x[n] + b1·x[n−1] + b2·x[n−2] − a1·y[n−1] − a2·y[n−2]
328	    ///
329	    /// `a0` is 1 in both of the standard's tables and is not carried.
330	    ///
331	    /// Double, not Float, and deliberately: the second stage's poles sit at
332	    /// a1 = −1.99005, a2 = 0.99007 — a hair from DC — and a single-precision
333	    /// direct form I loses enough per step to drift audibly over a
334	    /// forty-minute programme. This is not the audio render thread, so the
335	    /// precision is free.
336	    private struct Biquad {
337	        let b0: Double, b1: Double, b2: Double, a1: Double, a2: Double
338	    }
339	
340	    /// Table 1: "Filter coefficients for stage 1 of the pre-filter to model a
341	    /// spherical head" — a high shelf, +4 dB above about 2 kHz. Quoted from
342	    /// Recommendation ITU-R BS.1770-4 (10/2015), for 48 kHz.
343	    private static let stage1 = Biquad(
344	        b0: 1.535_124_859_586_97,
345	        b1: -2.691_696_189_406_38,
346	        b2: 1.198_392_810_852_85,
347	        a1: -1.690_659_293_182_41,
348	        a2: 0.732_480_774_215_85)
349	
350	    /// Table 2: "Filter coefficients for the second stage weighting curve" —
351	    /// the RLB high-pass. Same source, same rate.
352	    private static let stage2 = Biquad(
353	        b0: 1.0,
354	        b1: -2.0,
355	        b2: 1.0,
356	        a1: -1.990_047_454_833_98,
357	        a2: 0.990_072_250_366_21)
358	
359	    // ---- true peak -------------------------------------------------------
360	
361	    /// Taps per phase of the interpolating FIR.
362	    private static let peakTaps = 12
363	    private static let peakPhases = 4
364	
365	    /// Annex 2, § 3: "One set of filter coefficients (for the order 48,
366	    /// 4-phase, FIR interpolating) that would satisfy the requirements would
367	    /// be as follows", transcribed COLUMN BY COLUMN from the standard's own
368	    /// table — phase 0 first, tap 0 first — so it can be read back against
369	    /// the printed page a row at a time.
370	    ///
371	    /// Phase 3 is phase 0 reversed and phase 2 is phase 1 reversed, which is
372	    /// the linear-phase symmetry a correct transcription has and a mistyped
373	    /// one does not; the file's header records the DC gains the four phases
374	    /// actually have, which is the check that is NOT satisfied and is a
375	    /// property of the standard's set rather than of this copy of it.
376	    ///
377	    /// The standard's first processing step, a 12.04 dB attenuation, is
378	    /// omitted on the standard's own instruction: "This step is not necessary
379	    /// if the calculations are performed in floating point." So is the
380	    /// matching amplification, which is what it was for.
381	    private static let peakFilter: [[Double]] = [
382	        [
383	            0.001_708_984_375_0, 0.010_986_328_125_0, -0.019_653_320_312_5,
384	            0.033_203_125_000_0, -0.059_448_242_187_5, 0.137_329_101_562_5,
385	            0.972_167_968_750_0, -0.102_294_921_875_0, 0.047_607_421_875_0,
386	            -0.026_611_328_125_0, 0.014_892_578_125_0, -0.008_300_781_250_0,
387	        ],
388	        [
389	            -0.029_174_804_687_5, 0.029_296_875_000_0, -0.051_757_812_500_0,
390	            0.089_111_328_125_0, -0.166_503_906_250_0, 0.465_087_890_625_0,
391	            0.779_785_156_250_0, -0.200_317_382_812_5, 0.101_562_500_000_0,
392	            -0.058_227_539_062_5, 0.033_081_054_687_5, -0.018_920_898_437_5,
393	        ],
394	        [
395	            -0.018_920_898_437_5, 0.033_081_054_687_5, -0.058_227_539_062_5,
396	            0.101_562_500_000_0, -0.200_317_382_812_5, 0.779_785_156_250_0,
397	            0.465_087_890_625_0, -0.166_503_906_250_0, 0.089_111_328_125_0,
398	            -0.051_757_812_500_0, 0.029_296_875_000_0, -0.029_174_804_687_5,
399	        ],
400	        [
401	            -0.008_300_781_250_0, 0.014_892_578_125_0, -0.026_611_328_125_0,
402	            0.047_607_421_875_0, -0.102_294_921_875_0, 0.972_167_968_750_0,
403	            0.137_329_101_562_5, -0.059_448_242_187_5, 0.033_203_125_000_0,
404	            -0.019_653_320_312_5, 0.010_986_328_125_0, 0.001_708_984_375_0,
405	        ],
406	    ]
407	
408	    // ---- shape -----------------------------------------------------------
409	
410	    private let channelCount: Int
411	    /// Frames in one 100 ms sub-block, and the largest chunk `process`
412	    /// handles: a chunk never straddles a sub-block boundary, which is what
413	    /// lets one accumulator serve every channel.
414	    private let hopFrames: Int
415	    private let blockFrames: Int
416	
417	    /// One channel's samples for the current chunk, with the previous
418	    /// chunk's last 11 frames in front of them — the history the
419	    /// interpolating FIR needs across a buffer edge, and the reason a
420	    /// per-buffer implementation misses every inter-sample peak that
421	    /// straddles one (buffer edges arrive about a thousand times a minute).
422	    private let channelBuffer: UnsafeMutablePointer<Double>
423	    /// One phase's interpolated output for the current chunk.
424	    private let phaseBuffer: UnsafeMutablePointer<Double>
425	    /// `peakTaps − 1` raw samples per channel, carried between chunks.
426	    private let peakHistory: UnsafeMutablePointer<Double>
427	    /// Four coefficients per phase, REVERSED, because `vDSP_convD` computes
428	    /// a correlation (`C[n] = Σ A[n+p]·F[p]`) and a filter is the same sum
429	    /// with the taps the other way round. Derived here rather than typed
430	    /// again, so the literal above stays the only transcription.
431	    private let peakCoefficients: UnsafeMutablePointer<Double>
432	    /// Two sections of `x[n−1], x[n−2], y[n−1], y[n−2]`, per channel.
433	    private let filterState: UnsafeMutablePointer<Double>
434	    /// Int16 arrives from the fallback decode; the converted floats land
435	    /// here. `nil` until something asks, since the float path never does.
436	    private var int16Scratch: UnsafeMutablePointer<Float>?
437	    private var int16Capacity = 0
438	
439	    /// Σ over channels of Σ y² for the sub-block being filled.
440	    private var subBlockSum: Double = 0
441	    private var subBlockFilled = 0
442	    /// The last four sub-block sums, oldest overwritten.
443	    private var ring: [Double]
444	    private var ringWrites = 0
445	    /// One `Σᵢ Gᵢ·zᵢ` per completed 400 ms block. 100 ms apart, so ten a
446	    /// second — 36 000 doubles for an hour of programme, which is why the
447	    /// two-sweep gating can keep them all.
448	    private var blocks: [Double] = []
449	
450	    private var truePeakLinear: Double = 0
451	    private var samplePeakLinear: Double = 0
452	
453	    /// nil for a rate the coefficients are not published at, or a channel
454	    /// count this build cannot weight.
455	    ///
456	    /// **Both refusals are assertions, not conveniences.** The K-weighting
457	    /// table is 48 kHz only, and filtering at another rate would answer a
458	    /// number that looks right and is not. And BS.1770-4's Table 3 weights
459	    /// the surround channels 1.41 and excludes the LFE, which needs a
460	    /// channel LAYOUT this meter is not handed; mono and stereo are the two
461	    /// cases whose weights are all 1.0 and therefore need no layout, and the
462	    /// export mix is stereo by `ExportWriter.decodedAudioSettings`. A
463	    /// surround measurement is a feature, not a widening of this guard.
464	    init?(sampleRate: Double, channelCount: Int) {
465	        guard sampleRate == Self.requiredSampleRate, (1...2).contains(channelCount) else {
466	            return nil
467	        }
468	        self.channelCount = channelCount
469	        hopFrames = Int((sampleRate * Self.hopSeconds).rounded())
470	        blockFrames = hopFrames * Self.subBlocksPerBlock
471	        guard hopFrames > Self.peakTaps else { return nil }
472	
473	        let taps = Self.peakTaps
474	        channelBuffer = .allocate(capacity: hopFrames + taps - 1)
475	        channelBuffer.initialize(repeating: 0, count: hopFrames + taps - 1)
476	        phaseBuffer = .allocate(capacity: hopFrames)
477	        phaseBuffer.initialize(repeating: 0, count: hopFrames)
478	        peakHistory = .allocate(capacity: channelCount * (taps - 1))
479	        peakHistory.initialize(repeating: 0, count: channelCount * (taps - 1))
480	        peakCoefficients = .allocate(capacity: Self.peakPhases * taps)
481	        peakCoefficients.initialize(repeating: 0, count: Self.peakPhases * taps)
482	        for (index, phase) in Self.peakFilter.enumerated() {
483	            for (tap, value) in phase.reversed().enumerated() {
484	                peakCoefficients[index * taps + tap] = value
485	            }
486	        }
487	        filterState = .allocate(capacity: channelCount * 8)
488	        filterState.initialize(repeating: 0, count: channelCount * 8)
489	        ring = Array(repeating: 0, count: Self.subBlocksPerBlock)
490	    }
491	
492	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
493	        fatalError("LoudnessMeter does not support NSCoder")
494	    }
495	
496	    deinit {
497	        channelBuffer.deallocate()
498	        phaseBuffer.deallocate()
499	        peakHistory.deallocate()
500	        peakCoefficients.deallocate()
501	        filterState.deallocate()
502	        int16Scratch?.deallocate()
503	    }
504	
505	    // MARK: - Feeding
506	
507	    /// `frames` interleaved frames of 32-bit float, in programme order.
508	    func feed(_ samples: UnsafePointer<Float>, frames: Int) {
509	        var offset = 0
510	        while offset < frames {
511	            // Never across a sub-block boundary, and never more than one
512	            // sub-block: the accumulator then belongs to exactly one
513	            // sub-block for the whole chunk, whichever channel is being
514	            // walked.
515	            let take = Swift.min(hopFrames - subBlockFilled, frames - offset)
516	            process(samples + offset * channelCount, frames: take)
517	            offset += take
518	        }
519	    }
520	
521	    /// The same, for the 16-bit fallback decode: `AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput`
522	    /// is asked for float first and this is what a refusal falls back to
523	    /// (`Exporter.measureAudioSettings`). Scaled by 1/32768 so full scale is
524	    /// 1.0, which is what every threshold above is expressed in.
525	    func feedInt16(_ samples: UnsafePointer<Int16>, frames: Int) {
526	        let count = frames * channelCount
527	        guard count > 0 else { return }
528	        if int16Capacity < count {
529	            int16Scratch?.deallocate()
530	            int16Scratch = .allocate(capacity: count)
531	            int16Capacity = count
532	        }
533	        guard let scratch = int16Scratch else { return }
534	        var scale = Float(1.0 / 32768.0)
535	        vDSP_vflt16(samples, 1, scratch, 1, vDSP_Length(count))
536	        vDSP_vsmul(scratch, 1, &scale, scratch, 1, vDSP_Length(count))
537	        feed(scratch, frames: frames)
538	    }
539	
540	    /// One chunk, wholly inside one sub-block.
541	    private func process(_ samples: UnsafePointer<Float>, frames: Int) {
542	        guard frames > 0 else { return }
543	        let taps = Self.peakTaps
544	        let history = taps - 1
545	        let stride = vDSP_Stride(channelCount)
546	
547	        var chunkPeak: Float = 0
548	        vDSP_maxmgv(samples, 1, &chunkPeak, vDSP_Length(frames * channelCount))
549	        samplePeakLinear = Swift.max(samplePeakLinear, Double(chunkPeak))
550	
551	        for channel in 0..<channelCount {
552	            // The channel's history, then its new samples: one contiguous
553	            // run of `history + frames` doubles, which is exactly what both
554	            // the interpolator and the biquads want.
555	            channelBuffer.update(from: peakHistory + channel * history, count: history)
556	            vDSP_vspdp(
557	                samples + channel, stride, channelBuffer + history, 1, vDSP_Length(frames))
558	
559	            // True peak, on the UNWEIGHTED samples. Feeding K-weighted ones
560	            // here is an easy wiring mistake and reads up to 4 dB high on
561	            // bright material.
562	            for phase in 0..<Self.peakPhases {
563	                vDSP_convD(
564	                    channelBuffer, 1, peakCoefficients + phase * taps, 1, phaseBuffer, 1,
565	                    vDSP_Length(frames), vDSP_Length(taps))
566	                var peak: Double = 0
567	                vDSP_maxmgvD(phaseBuffer, 1, &peak, vDSP_Length(frames))
568	                truePeakLinear = Swift.max(truePeakLinear, peak)
569	            }
570	
571	            // Before the filtering, which overwrites the same run: the last
572	            // `history` RAW samples are the next chunk's history.
573	            (peakHistory + channel * history).update(
574	                from: channelBuffer + frames, count: history)
575	
576	            weight(channelBuffer + history, frames: frames, channel: channel)
577	            var sum: Double = 0
578	            vDSP_svesqD(channelBuffer + history, 1, &sum, vDSP_Length(frames))
579	            // Table 3's Gᵢ is 1.0 for left, right and centre, so the sum over
580	            // channels needs no weight at all here; `init` is where the
581	            // channel counts that would need one are refused.
582	            subBlockSum += sum
583	        }
584	
585	        subBlockFilled += frames
586	        if subBlockFilled >= hopFrames { closeSubBlock() }
587	    }
588	
589	    /// The two-stage K-weighting, in place, with this channel's state.
590	    private func weight(_ samples: UnsafeMutablePointer<Double>, frames: Int, channel: Int) {
591	        let base = filterState + channel * 8
592	        for (index, section) in [Self.stage1, Self.stage2].enumerated() {
593	            let state = base + index * 4
594	            var x1 = state[0], x2 = state[1], y1 = state[2], y2 = state[3]
595	            for n in 0..<frames {
596	                let x = samples[n]
597	                let y = section.b0 * x + section.b1 * x1 + section.b2 * x2
598	                    - section.a1 * y1 - section.a2 * y2
599	                x2 = x1
600	                x1 = x
601	                y2 = y1
602	                y1 = y
603	                samples[n] = y
604	            }
605	            state[0] = x1
606	            state[1] = x2
607	            state[2] = y1
608	            state[3] = y2
609	        }
610	    }
611	
612	    private func closeSubBlock() {
613	        ring[ringWrites % Self.subBlocksPerBlock] = subBlockSum
614	        ringWrites += 1
615	        subBlockSum = 0
616	        subBlockFilled = 0
617	        guard ringWrites >= Self.subBlocksPerBlock else { return }
618	        blocks.append(ring.reduce(0, +) / Double(blockFrames))
619	    }
620	
621	    // MARK: - The answer
622	
623	    /// The gated integrated loudness and the true peak.
624	    ///
625	    /// A trailing partial block is discarded, which the standard requires and
626	    /// which means a programme shorter than 400 ms has no integrated loudness
627	    /// at all.
628	    ///
629	    /// **A non-finite sample is not defended against here**, and what it does
630	    /// is worth knowing before someone reads a strange number as a bug in the
631	    /// filter: a NaN is dropped by both peak accumulators (`Swift.max` keeps
632	    /// the accumulator when the new value is NaN) but poisons the biquad
633	    /// state, so every later block is NaN and is dropped by `integrated`'s
634	    /// `$0 > 0`, leaving the integrated figure that of the programme up to
635	    /// that sample; an infinity survives into `truePeakDBTP` as +∞. Neither
636	    /// is silently normalised, and neither can push a file up:
637	    /// `ExportLoudness.resolve` reads a non-finite peak as NO headroom, and
638	    /// `summary` says the peak could not be measured rather than calling the
639	    /// programme silent.
640	    func finish() -> LoudnessReport {
641	        let peak = Swift.max(truePeakLinear, samplePeakLinear)
642	        return LoudnessReport(
643	            integratedLUFS: integrated(),
644	            truePeakDBTP: Self.decibels(peak),
645	            samplePeakDBFS: Self.decibels(samplePeakLinear))
646	    }
647	
648	    /// BS.1770-4 equations (5)–(7): the absolute gate, then the relative one,
649	    /// applied ONCE.
650	    ///
651	    /// The mean is over the LINEAR mean squares, never over the block
652	    /// loudnesses. Both gates are expressed in dB, which invites averaging
653	    /// dB; the gates only SELECT blocks, and the answer is the loudness of
654	    /// the survivors' linear mean.
655	    private func integrated() -> Double? {
656	        let gated = blocks.filter { $0 > 0 && Self.loudness($0) > Self.absoluteGate }
657	        guard !gated.isEmpty else { return nil }
658	        let threshold = Self.loudness(gated.reduce(0, +) / Double(gated.count))
659	            + Self.relativeGate
660	        let kept = gated.filter { Self.loudness($0) > threshold }
661	        guard !kept.isEmpty else { return nil }
662	        return Self.loudness(kept.reduce(0, +) / Double(kept.count))
663	    }
664	
665	    /// A weighted mean square as a loudness, BS.1770-4 equation (2).
666	    private static func loudness(_ meanSquare: Double) -> Double {
667	        guard meanSquare > 0 else { return -.infinity }
668	        return offset + 10 * log10(meanSquare)
669	    }
670	
671	    private static func decibels(_ linear: Double) -> Double {
672	        linear > 0 ? 20 * log10(linear) : -.infinity
673	    }
674	}

- **SY-42 — Every reader of an MP3 reads past the encoder delay Core Audio leaves in (#309;
  amends SY-38's residue).** Recorded in clean-up round 3 (batch A, 2026-10-22) before its code,
  from the owner's "queue the other bugs … fix them in batches" of that day; its numbers are the
  implementer's printed run of 2026-10-22 (`export_offset_proof.py --only …,X16,X17`). SY-38 left
  peaks, speech, the transcription extract and the reverse reading an MP3's sound `encoderDelay`
  frames late wherever `MP3Gapless.leadingTrim` is past zero — 13.061 ms at 44.1 kHz and 12.000
  ms at 48 kHz (MPEG-1, accepted under 16.7 ms), 24 ms at 24 kHz (MPEG-2, over it). Each now
  takes the same trim, as a placement and not only a read range: **peaks**
  (`MediaImporter.writePeaks`) decode from 0 and `PeakBuckets` places every buffer, and counts
  its coverage, at PTS − trim, so the priming falls before bucket 0 under the existing `bucket >=
  0` rule; the coverage the publish asks for is `peaksRanges(expected, less: trim)`, the track's
  ranges shifted by −trim and cut at 0. **Speech** (`MediaImporter.speechReader`, `writeSpeech`'s
  reader) starts its reader at the trim; the probabilities stay placed by index from 0, so chunk
  0 is the recording's first 32 ms. **The transcription extract** (`Transcriber.extractAudio`)
  reads `range` shifted by the trim and starts its writer's session there, so the extract's frame
  0 is the recording's `range.start` for a clip's window and the cloud upload alike. **The
  reverse** (`ReverseRenderer`) reads each slice at `[start + trim, cursor + trim)` and opens the
  reversed file with the trim's frames of silence (the recording's last stretch lies past the
  decode's end); `leadingTrim` answers only for a bare MPEG stream, so no picture is ever
  shifted. A file with no trim — every non-MP3, an MP3 with a packet table or no tag — reads
  byte-identically to before in all four. **Versions:** the peaks marker's `version` is 2, the
  speech marker carries `version` 2 (a marker without it fails to decode), and
  `ReverseCache.rendererVersion` is 5: every peaks, speech and reverse cache is made again once,
  SY-34's no-migration posture; the MPEG-1 residues SY-38 accepted go with the MPEG-2 one. **A
  cloud transcript already cached for an MP3 is not re-fetched:** re-fetching spends, and its
  words stay where that upload placed them until the owner asks for a new transcript. **The
  pins:** X16 reads the product's speech reader, extract and reverse of clicks24-mp3,
  clicks44-mp3, clicks48-mp3 and the WAVs clicks44 and clicks48, each pinned by SY-27 (≥ 10 of 12
  found, |median| ≤ 1.0 ms, spread ≤ 0.5 ms); every read found 12 of 12 — speech −0.042 / −0.085
  / −0.042 ms (controls −0.023 / −0.042), the extract −0.042 / −0.023 / −0.042 (−0.023 / −0.042),
  the reverse +0.667 / +0.377 / −0.000 (+0.377 / +0.000), spread 0.000 throughout. X17 reads the
  published peaks `.bin` of the same five by whole buckets (the clicks sit on 10 ms bucket
  boundaries, so a millisecond median would flip a bucket on a one-sample decode shift): for a
  click at t, e = b − round(t·100), b the loudest bucket within ±6, pinned per fixture to ≥ 10
  found and every e in {−1, 0}; all five read e = 0 on 12 of 12, where the untrimmed lag puts
  every click at e ≥ +1. Mutants M19–M24 (each reader's trim removed, the reverse's silence
  skipped, the shifted coverage not asked for) must each fail their row, M19 on each of the three
  MP3s. L11 stays SY-38's record of the untrimmed decodes.
